vulnerabilities.description: Garmin login exception handler exposes password. If GarminClient() raises exception containing password, full exception message is transmitted via Telegram without sanitization. Malicious garminconnect library or network error with credentials in message leaks password to Telegram.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Catch exceptions by type only; never include full message when credentials involved. Use msg='Garmin login failed'; telegram(msg) without exception object.

vulnerabilities.description: API key and access token exposure via error responses. If intervals.icu or Strava returns error response containing the API key/token, it gets exposed in thrown errors and potentially logged to browser console/dev tools.
vulnerabilities.impact: API credentials exposed in error logs accessible to browser dev tools
vulnerabilities.remediation: Strip sensitive headers/tokens from error response bodies before exposing. Use generic error message instead of res.text() verbatim.

vulnerabilities.description: Strava access token exposure via error response body. Same as intervals.icu issue — error text not sanitized before throwing.
vulnerabilities.impact: Strava token exposed in error logs
vulnerabilities.remediation: Sanitize error responses; do not expose third-party API error messages directly.

vulnerabilities.description: No rate limiting on /garmin/login endpoint. Unlike /auth/login (1-second sleep enforced), Garmin login allows unlimited concurrent attempts. Authenticated user could spam endpoint to trigger 429s and exhaust Garmin retry budget.
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of service against Garmin API quota
vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply _LOGIN_BRAKE pattern to Garmin login endpoint. Add 1-second delay between attempts per session/email.

vulnerabilities.description: No rate limiting on /garmin/mfa endpoint. MFA code submission has no braking, allowing unlimited brute-force attempts against 6-digit TOTP codes.
vulnerabilities.impact: Brute-force attack on MFA codes (1 in 1,000,000 odds per attempt)
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add rate limiting per email/session. Max 3-5 attempts per minute. Lock session after 10 failures for 15 minutes.

vulnerabilities.description: sessionStorage credentials readable by XSS within same origin. API keys and Strava tokens stored in sessionStorage (correctly ephemeral), but XSS in bike module could read and exfiltrate tokens.
vulnerabilities.impact: XSS in bike tab could steal API credentials for current browser session
vulnerabilities.remediation: Acceptable trade-off for serverless app. SessionStorage prevents disk persistence. Further mitigation requires server-side token proxy (adds backend). Monitor for XSS vulnerabilities in bike module code.

vulnerabilities.description: Unconventional use of bitwise operators in check_login() password verification. While technically constant-time correct (both checks use | and &), using bitwise operators on booleans instead of logical operators is confusing and fragile.
vulnerabilities.impact: Code maintainability risk; timing-safe comparison could regress if refactored
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use logical 'and'/'or' operators for clarity; verify timing-safety is maintained. Add comment explaining timing-attack mitigation.

recommendations.action: Fix Garmin password exposure in runner.py:278
recommendations.details: Replace exception message transmission with generic error string. Never pass exception object to Telegram.
Parse response.status only. Use generic 'Upload failed' message instead of response.text(). Log errors internally (console) without exposing to user-facing throws.

recommendations.action: Add rate limiting to Garmin endpoints
recommendations.details: Implement token bucket or sliding window on /garmin/login and /garmin/mfa. Max 3 attempts/min per session. Track by session ID and email. Return 429 Too Many Requests.
After 10 failed MFA code entries, lock session for 15 minutes. Notify user of lockout. Clear lock after successful login.
Add comment to view.js explaining trade-off: sessionStorage clears on browser close (good) but is readable by same-origin XSS (acceptable for serverless, requires server proxy for mitigation).
Replace bitwise operators with logical operators in check_login(). Add 'constant-time comparison' comment explaining why 'and' is used instead of short-circuit evaluation.

positiveFindings: No XSS in browser code (escHtml() applied consistently)
No CSRF (stateful server sessions with SameSite cookies)
Session tokens use secrets.token_urlsafe(32) with HttpOnly + Secure flags
API credentials stored in ephemeral sessionStorage, not localStorage
Credentials never persisted to state (per design)
summary: Garmin password exposure in exception handling is critical and requires immediate fix. API error response sanitization is high priority. Rate limiting gaps on Garmin auth endpoints are the most actionable hardening opportunity. Overall security posture is strong for a serverless application; no SQL injection, XSS, or path traversal vulnerabilities found.
